title: The Freebie Audiobook Directory
subtitle: Legal free audiobooks, explained like a friend would

sources.name: LibriVox
sources.device: Any web browser, podcast apps (Apple Podcasts, Spotify, etc.), iOS/Android apps, smart speakers
sources.review: Volunteers narrating every public-domain classic — the quality is a grab-bag, but the price is exactly right.

sources.name: Libby (with your library card)
sources.device: iOS, Android, Fire tablets, any web browser, Apple CarPlay / Android Auto
sources.review: Real new-release audiobooks, free, straight through the library card you already own — just expect a waitlist on the hot titles.
sources.cost: Free with a library card (holds queue, ~20 loans at a time depending on library)

sources.name: Hoopla (with your library card)
sources.device: iOS, Android, web browsers, Roku/Apple TV/Android TV, Apple CarPlay / Android Auto
sources.review: Libby's no-wait sibling: instant borrows every month, so grab the niche titles here and let Libby handle the bestsellers.
sources.cost: Free with a library card (limited monthly borrows, instant checkout, no holds)

sources.name: Internet Archive: Audio Books & Poetry
sources.device: Any web browser; downloadable MP3s for offline play on any device
sources.review: A giant attic of public-domain readings and LibriVox mirrors — dusty, un-looked-after, and full of treasures you won't find anywhere else.

sources.name: Loyal Books
sources.device: Any web browser, iOS/Android app, podcast apps
sources.review: LibriVox with friendlier packaging plus its own picks — the easiest first stop if app-based browsing beats digging through archives.

sources.name: Lit2Go
sources.device: Any web browser, podcast apps (iTunes feed), downloadable MP3s
sources.review: An educator-run reading collection with printable transcripts and reading levels — weirdly great for ESL learners and kids.

sources.name: Open Culture: Free Audiobooks
sources.device: Any web browser (links out to MP3s and podcast feeds that play anywhere)
sources.review: A curated list of 1,000+ free classic audiobooks — the connoisseur's shortcut when you want the cream skimmed for you.

sources.name: Welcome to Night Vale
sources.device: Podcast apps (Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pocket Casts, etc.), any web browser
sources.review: Community radio from a desert town where every conspiracy is true — the reigning king of free podcast fiction, period.
sources.cost: Back catalog free in podcast apps; paid live events and books exist but are optional

sources.name: The Magnus Archives (Rusty Quill)
sources.device: Podcast apps, any web browser, offline via podcast downloads
sources.review: Starts as spooky-but-tidy horror stories, quietly knits itself into one of the best long-form audio dramas ever made.
sources.cost: Back catalog free in podcast apps; ad-free/early-access tiers are optional

sources.name: Escape Pod
sources.device: Podcast apps, any web browser, downloadable MP3s
sources.review: Weekly free science-fiction short fiction read aloud — magazine-quality stories in bookshelf-sized listening bites.

sources.name: Audible free trial
sources.device: iOS, Android, Windows/Mac apps, CarPlay/Android Auto, Fire tablets, Sonos — widest device coverage anywhere
sources.review: The trial is genuinely free for 30 days and lands 1 credit, so binge one big audiobook for nothing, then set a reminder to cancel the same day you sign up.
sources.cost: 30 days free (typically 1 credit), then a monthly subscription
sources.verdict: Worth it — if you cancel the same day you sign up; skipping is fine because Libby covers most new releases anyway.

sources.name: Spotify Premium
sources.device: iOS, Android, web, desktop apps, game consoles, smart speakers — basically everything
sources.review: Premium includes a monthly audiobook listening allowance alongside every song ever, so trial it and see if the bundle actually fits your ears.
sources.cost: Free tier exists (ads, shuffle); Premium trial available; Premium includes an audiobook-hours allowance
sources.verdict: Worth trying — the music bundle means it almost certainly won't go to waste; check current audiobook terms on the signup page.

sources.name: Everand (formerly Scribd)
sources.device: iOS, Android, any web browser, offline downloads
sources.review: It's Netflix-shaped for books, but with a smaller library than Spotify or Libby — trial only if you can already name three titles you'd finish this month.
sources.cost: Free trial available, then a monthly subscription
sources.verdict: Skippable — unless you already have a binge list, Libby and Hoopla will fill in fine.

sources.name: Chirp
sources.device: iOS, Android, web player, Apple CarPlay / Android Auto
sources.review: Not a trial at all: a free app that blasts daily $0.99-$4.99 audiobook deals to your inbox, no subscription ever.
sources.cost: Free app and accounts; you just buy the deals you want
sources.verdict: Worth keeping — the only entry here with zero strings and zero guilt.
